messages:
lina: Hey team — customer (Acme) reports intermittent SSE disconnects and lots of partial output when requests route through ALB + Cloudflare. They see reconnect loops from the client and a billing spike. Repro steps attached, logs below. Can eng help triage?

lina: Symptoms: 1) initial SSE chunk(s) arrive, then silence for ~30s, connection reset, client reconnects. 2) Some responses end with truncated event (no trailing newline). 3) Billing shows repeated short requests (reconnects).

lina: Quick repro curl they used:
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \  "https://api.redwood-hosted.example.com/v1/streams/chat?model=xlarge"
```

lina: ALB target logs: repeated 502/504 around the time of silence. Cloudflare shows Origin Connect Timeouts and some 524s.

samir: thanks — do we have a pcap or full tcpdump from the origin during a repro? curious if it's half-close or proxy buffering.

lina: customer attached small pcap and nginx/gunicorn access logs. pcap shows FIN from client after long silence; origin sent last chunk but it seems not flushed to socket.

maya: re: proxy buffering — ALB and Cloudflare both can buffer or interrupt long-lived responses depending on idle timeouts. ALB default idle timeout is 60s, Cloudflare has edge keepalive semantics. If the runtime doesn't emit periodic keepalives, proxies may consider the connection stalled.

samir: Agreed. Our runtime uses chunked transfer and writes tokens as they come, but if the application-level flush doesn't hit the kernel due to Nagle or stdio buffering, the proxy can coalesce or drop. Two things to check: 1) ensure server sends small heartbeat chunks (e.g., "\n: keepalive\n\n") every 15s; 2) set TCP_NODELAY and flush after each write.

aaron: Also check ALB idle timeout config on the customer's side. We had a case where ALB was 30s and client keepalives were at 60s -> disconnects. Recommend aligning keepalive < min(idle_timeouts).

lina: Customer says they already set keepalives in app but still see truncation when Cloudflare in front. Could Cloudflare's edge close cause partial last chunk?

samir: Yes. Cloudflare can return 524/502 if the origin doesn't respond within the edge timeout. Additionally Cloudflare may buffer a bit; if it receives a final EOF from origin but the last chunk header/tailer is incomplete, the client sees truncated event.

maya: Workaround: for Cloudflare customers, enable "Origin Keep-alive" and increase origin response timeout; also set "Cache: no-transform" and correct content-type (text/event-stream) so intermediaries avoid rewriting.

samir: Repro suggestion for us to validate: run a local ALB/NLB + cloudflare-worker mimic and curl with --no-buffer while we instrument kernel-level tcpdump on the origin. Collect timestamps for: first byte from origin -> packet leaving origin -> packet arriving at edge -> client disconnect.

lina: Pasted customer's nginx config snippet (sanitized):
```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_set_header Connection keep-alive;
proxy_set_header Host $host;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```

samir: proxy_buffering off is good. But check upstream keepalive_timeout and sendfile/off settings. If using uWSGI/gunicorn behind nginx, ensure their worker send_chunks or flush settings are set.

aaron: We should also look at ALB/LB health check behavior: some customers route SSE traffic through a listener that is also used for short requests; when targets are drained the ALB may half-close connections.

lina: From customer logs: 
- 2026-03-01T14:02:11Z SSE started
- 2026-03-01T14:02:34Z last token sent from runtime
- 2026-03-01T14:02:45Z Cloudflare logs: origin timeout -> 524
- 2026-03-01T14:02:46Z client reconnect

samir: That pattern smells like an idle probe/timeout on the edge at ~30s. Let's try forcing a 10s heartbeat chunk from runtime to see if it stabilizes. I can patch a test build that injects keepalive every 10s.

maya: I'll ask infra to spin a repro environment with ALB idle=30s / ALB idle=60s and Cloudflare-like worker to compare.

lina: Customer asked about billing: they want to avoid reconnect loops billing them for repeated partial streams. Any short-term mitigations?

aaron: Short-term: implement a client-side exponential backoff with jitter and a max-charge cutoff (e.g., if reconnects > X per minute, throttle / switch to polling). Also consider server-side session resume tokens so reconnects can resume where they left off instead of restarting full generation.

samir: On our side, we can improve graceful EOF: ensure we always end SSE events with a blank line and flush, e.g., send "\ndata: <chunk>\n\n" and call fsync/socket flush before closing. That reduces the chance of partial final events.

lina: plan: 1) samir will build keepalive-test binary (injects 10s heartbeats) and share a test endpoint by EOD. 2) maya will provision ALB/CF repro env and collect tcpdumps. 3) aaron will draft customer-facing mitigation steps (client backoff + resume token pattern).

lina: ops-bot: create ticket for customer escalation?

ops-bot: Ticket created: #INC-2026-1849 — assigned to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:

samir: noted. I'll post test endpoint once build is up. :eyes:

lina: thanks all — keeping customer in loop. :thumbsup:
